name: James Talarico
role: Texas state representative (2018–present); 2026 Democratic U.S. Senate nominee
summary: Talarico is a Texas legislator, former teacher and Christian seminarian who frames politics as a conflict between concentrated wealth and ordinary people. His legislative record includes abortion-access proposals and emissions-reduction targets; his interviews advocate universal health coverage, competitive markets, stronger public schools, church-state separation and support for Ukraine and NATO.

notes: Later pass checked every statement, including candidates. Searched economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means and globalism in the full Rogan and CNN interviews and retrieved legislative material. The MediaSum corpus returned zero Talarico transcripts; the local reference library has no book by him, and US Congress/foreign-parliament corpora do not cover a Texas state representative. Campaign pages s4–s11 and The Reload s13 returned HTTP 403 and were not retried; GitHub repository/code searches found no mirror. The tech issue page also returned 403. Sources s2 and the blocked pages survive only to document earlier versions. Source s17a refers only to the record section of the same page as words source s17. The CNN town hall clarifies several earlier claims; recent words do not replace legislative actions. Follow-up searches addressed secession, territorial autonomy, minority-language provision, supranational institutions and executive checks. They did not yield additional qualifying positions on those statements. A Diary of a CEO transcript also returned HTTP 403 and was not retried. ATPE’s complete 2022/2024 survey responses were read as primary words, and the linked House Journals were checked for voucher and library-book votes. These vote documents replace interview claims wherever they settle the same statement. No further qualifying evidence was found for the remaining thin themes. Source s3a separately identifies the health-care page’s report of legislative actions; those reported actions, at medium confidence, replace campaign promises on corporate regulation and welfare cuts. The AP election-result page also refused access with HTTP 403.
